title: Radio Announcement: Bramley Farmers' Market
context: A presenter on a local community radio station announces details of an upcoming farmers' market.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: And now for some local news. Bramley Farmers' Market is returning to the town square this month, and organisers say it will be the biggest one yet.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: It's organised by the Bramley Traders' Association, who've been running it for years, and this year they've promised a few extra surprises for regular visitors.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The market normally runs on the last Saturday of the month, but this time, because of the town's summer festival, it's been moved forward to the third Saturday instead.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Do make a note of that in your diary, because it really is a different date from usual, and quite a few people get caught out by it every year.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: It opens at nine a.m. and organisers say to expect over forty stalls this year, up from around twenty-five last year, selling everything from fresh vegetables to homemade bread.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: That growth is largely down to a new wave of small producers from just outside the town who've asked to join this year.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Entry to the market is free, though of course you'll want to bring some cash, as a lot of the smaller stallholders don't take card payments.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: There is a cash machine near the church at the edge of the square, though organisers say it does sometimes run out on a busy morning, so it's worth coming prepared.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: One new addition this year is a small stage in the corner of the square, where local musicians will perform between eleven and one, so do stick around after your shopping.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: This week's line-up includes a folk duo and a local school choir, so there should be something for everyone, whatever your taste in music. There's no need to book a seat, just wander over whenever you fancy a sit-down.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: If you're driving, the usual advice is to park at the multi-storey on Fern Street, but I'm told that's actually closed for repairs this month, so instead the council is opening the school car park on Barton Road for market visitors.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: It's a short walk from there into the square, about the same distance as from the usual car park, so it shouldn't add much time to your visit.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: That car park will be free until midday, and then a small charge of two pounds applies for the rest of the day.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: For anyone who can't make it in person, a few of the regular stallholders, including the cheese stall and the honey stall, are now taking online orders for local delivery, and you'll find links to both on our website.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: A couple of the other stallholders are hoping to set up the same sort of service before too long, so keep an eye on the website for updates.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Organisers are also looking for volunteers to help set up the stalls early in the morning, and in return you'll get a free hot drink and a bacon roll from the café van.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: It's a lovely way to feel part of the event, and organisers say many of last year's volunteers have already put their names down again. You don't need any experience at all, just a willingness to carry a few crates.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: If you'd like to volunteer, just turn up at seven thirty on the day, right by the fountain in the square, where the organiser will be waiting with a list.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Dogs are welcome at the market this year, on a lead, though organisers ask that you keep them away from the food stalls specifically, out of respect for other shoppers.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Water bowls will be put out near the entrance as well, for any thirsty dogs who've worked up an appetite from all the walking.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: There's also a small children's area this time, with face painting and a short puppet show, which should keep younger visitors entertained while the adults browse the stalls.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: If the weather turns bad, don't worry — the market has a wet-weather plan, and stalls will simply move under the covered market hall next to the square rather than being cancelled.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: It's happened once or twice in past years, and organisers say the covered hall works just as well, if a little cosier than being out in the open.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: That's Bramley Farmers' Market, the third Saturday of this month, from nine until two. More local news after the break.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: So, plenty to look forward to this year at Bramley Farmers' Market. We'll have more details on our website.
